samples.summary: Merge cleanup adds a second store write, splitting a single Backspace-merge into two Yorkie undo units
samples.evidence: `mergeBlocks` now does `store.mergeBlock(...)` followed by `dropStaleStyleOff(blockId)` → `store.applyStyles(...)`. Under `YorkieDocStore` each of those is its own `doc.update()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2275 for the merge, :1806 for applyStyles) and `snapshot()` is a documented no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729), so undo granularity is tied to the write. The same commit's comment in view/editor.ts:1049-1058 explicitly acknowledges this defect for the (rare) named-style path and defers it, but the merge path — the hottest editing path, per the new comment at document.ts:382-387 — gets the same second undo unit with no mention. Worse, `mergeBlock` undo is not even supported by Yorkie today (skipped test at packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:259-261), so after a Backspace that strands a flag the first Cmd+Z re-inserts `italic: false` into the already-merged paragraph — a state the user never had — rather than un-merging. Also, `consumePendingCursor()` is consumed by the merge update, so the cleanup update records no history presence and its undo restores no cursor.

samples.summary: `splitBlock` strands the same style-off flag the new merge sweep removes, and the sweep can never reach it (empty runs are skipped)
samples.evidence: Enter at the end of a Heading 6 takes the `newType = 'paragraph'` branch (document.ts:360-371). `applySplitBlock` copies the split-point style onto the empty side (`getSplitPointStyle`, block-helpers.ts:221-225, used at :269-270), so the new paragraph's empty run carries the `italic: false` that was a live Heading 6 override. Typing then inherits it (`applyInsertText` uses the run's style), producing exactly the dead flag #749 targets in a paragraph. `Doc.splitBlock` performs no `dropStaleStyleOff`, and even the document-wide sweep cannot pre-empt it: `collectStaleStyleOff` skips zero-length runs (`if (patch && end > pos)`, document.ts:554). Consequence: after a later 'Normal → italic' redefinition, `dropStaleStyleOffAll` reads that `false` as a live override (defaults.italic true) and silently refuses the redefinition on that run — the exact failure the merge fix was added to prevent. So the invariant the new comment asserts ('a stored `false` is only ever a live override') still does not hold.

samples.summary: Merge sweep runs a full block scan + possible extra store write on every merge in bulk delete loops
samples.evidence: `mergeBlocks` is called in loops from range-deletion paths (view/text-editor.ts:3243, :3345, :3411) and from `deleteBackward` (document.ts:320). Each call now adds a `refresh()`-backed scan of the destination block and, when anything is stale, a second `refresh()` plus an `applyStyles` write. In the Yorkie store that is an extra `doc.update()` per merged block in a bulk delete, i.e. N extra undo units for one user action; the batching guarantee in `writeStaleStyleOffEdits` only batches within a single merge, not across the loop.

Under `YorkieDocStore` each of those is its own `doc.update()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2275 for the merge, :1806 for applyStyles) and `snapshot()` is a documented no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729), so undo granularity is tied to the write. verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. document.ts:379-389 adds `dropStaleStyleOff(blockId)` after `store.mergeBlock(...)`, which routes through writeStaleStyleOffEdits (569-575) to a second `store.applyStyles(...)`. Under YorkieDocStore that is a distinct `doc.update()` (mergeBlock's at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2275, applyStyles' at :1806), and `snapshot()` is an explicit no-op (:2727-2729), so the editor's saveSnapshot() before Backspace (text-editor.ts:1937) cannot group them — the merge and its cleanup become two Yorkie undo units. The same commit's editor.ts:1039-1058 comment acknowledges exactly this consequence for the named-style path and defers it; the merge path gets no such acknowledgement. Because mergeBlock undo is itself unsupported (skipped test yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:259-269), the first Cmd+Z after a stranding Backspace re-inserts `italic: false` into the already-merged paragraph — a state the user never had — and applyStyles' consumePendingCursor() at :1805 returns nothing (mergeBlock consumed it at :2274), so that unit records no history presence and restores no cursor. No refutation ground applies: the code is present (not not-present), nothing guards it (snapshot() is a no-op and DocStore has no batch() seam, store.ts:48-49), and a user-visible wrong intermediate state / broken invariant is squarely in the correctness lane (not out-of-scope). The only overstatement is calling it unconditional on the merge path — the second write only fires when a stale flag actually exists (writeStaleStyleOffEdits returns false for zero edits) — which narrows frequency but not the defect.

mergedFrom.summary: Merge sweep runs a full block scan + possible extra store write on every merge in bulk delete loops
mergedFrom.evidence: `mergeBlocks` is called in loops from range-deletion paths (view/text-editor.ts:3243, :3345, :3411) and from `deleteBackward` (document.ts:320). Each call now adds a `refresh()`-backed scan of the destination block and, when anything is stale, a second `refresh()` plus an `applyStyles` write. verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and found no counterexample. Doc.splitBlock (document.ts:328-374) writes through store.splitBlock + refresh with no dropStaleStyleOff, unlike mergeBlocks (:388) and setBlockType (:618). applySplitBlock copies the split-point run style onto the empty side (block-helpers.ts:221-225, 268-270), and normalizeInlines preserves that fallback style (block-helpers.ts:105-111); the Yorkie store does the same (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2167-2174, 2233). heading-6 supplies italic:true (named-styles.ts:91), so styleOffAsClear legitimately stores italic:false there (document.ts:448-463) and Enter at end of a Heading 6 carries that false into a paragraph's empty run. Typing absorbs it (applyInsertText keeps inline.style, block-helpers.ts:117-139; Doc.insertText does no cleanup, document.ts:260-261; pending style only applies when armed, pending-style.ts:28-42). collectStaleStyleOff skips zero-length runs (document.ts:554), and the only redefinition-time sweep runs AFTER the new style table (editor.ts:1059-1063; dropStaleStyleOffAll refreshes first, document.ts:506-525), where defaults.italic===true makes it keep the flag (document.ts:549). Exhaustive search of the only mechanism that can distinguish false from absent (BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS used at document.ts:40,448,547) and of all dropStaleStyleOff* callers (setBlockType, mergeBlocks, internal paste text-editor.ts:1264, afterNamedStyleChange) turned up nothing on the Enter/split path (text-editor.ts:407-411, 2095, 2117, 2128, 2151). Minor overstatement in the finding: after typing the run is non-empty so an unrelated sweep could clear it, but no sweep runs on this path and the redefinition sweep preserves it — the invariant asserted in the new merge comment is broken.
